summary: 1. High-stayed videos (>65% stayed_pct) use Devanagari Hindi text with direct, counter-intuitive statements or vivid visual metaphors (e.g., 'car crash में पिचक जाती है', '3 छोटी cars दांतों पर'). 2. Top-performing hooks directly address the viewer using 'सोचो' (Imagine) or 'तुम' (You) within the first 3 words to instantly anchor attention. 3. Short, tight duration videos (14–17 second average view duration) dramatically outperform 40–50+ second standard-arm videos in reach and stayed percentage. 4. English and Hinglish titling/hooks (e.g., 'Common Household Items...') severely underperform compared to Hindi-script titles containing emojis and clear question/curiosity framing. 5. Videos that stall under 100 views suffer from passive, formal, or textbook-like opening sentences ('डायनासोर के जीवाश्मों में वैज्ञानिकों को...') instead of immediate punchy action.
winning_hooks: Start with vivid physical visualizer + 'सोचो'/'तुम' (e.g., 'सोचो, तुम्हारे दांतों पर 3 छोटी cars...').
Use counter-intuitive fact as statement #1 (e.g., 'जो car crash में पिचक जाती है, वो तुम्हें ज़्यादा बचाती है।').
Keep first sentence under 12 words with zero preamble or channel introductions.
avoid: Abstract or passive academic phrasing (e.g., 'वैज्ञानिकों को ऐसी सूक्ष्म आकृतियां क्यों मिली हैं...').
Pure English titles and Hinglish script hooks for technical topics (e.g., 'Common Household Items That Contain...').
Standard long-form script structures (>40s duration) before mastering initial 15-second retention.
next_experiment: Test Devanagari Hindi titles + 'सोचो' (Imagine) visual hooks vs direct counter-intuitive fact hooks across 5 videos capped under 20 seconds duration.
